queries.hook: The weight of a thing you keep trying and cannot make work, while the rest of your life takes up every hour you have left.
queries.diagnose: Doubt and delay feed each other; waiting to feel ready keeps us stuck, and the unacted-on decision weighs more than the work.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Do one small thing that is only for you, not for the result; let the day be enough and the work be enough.
queries.story: A man who tried many paths, failed at each, and found that the one who kept going was not the one who won, but the one who did not stop trying.

verse.speaker: Bhasa
verse.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
verse.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
verse.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verse.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
verse.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

verse.meaning: Bhasa and Vilasa meet as old men after years apart. One asks the other how he is. The other admits he has never found peace. He tells Bhasa that his mind is caught on endless lists, always running through what is done and what must come next. The mind is carried on great waves of tasks, never still. Its depths dance with worry. Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.
verse.for_you: You are running on empty. The doubt is not about the apps. You are carrying the exhaustion of a mind that never gets a moment's rest.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वेषां कर्मणां तात फले नित्यमनित्यता / अनित्यमिति जानन्तो न भवन्ति भवन्ति च अथ ये नैव कुर्वन्ति नैव जातु भवन्ति ते / ऐकगुण्यमनीहायामभावः कर्मणां फलम्
verse.line: Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.
verse.translation: The result of every action is uncertain. Knowing this, some people act and succeed, some do not. But those who never act never succeed at all.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after he has lost his kingdom. She tells him that the result of any action is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some do not. But those who never try never succeed at all. She wants him to see that waiting in despair is the only way to guarantee failure. The truth she offers is that trying is the only path, even when the outcome is unknown.
verse.for_you: You are lying in the same place Sanjaya did, defeated by the apps that have not worked. The truth underneath your exhaustion is not about the code. It is about the belief that trying and failing proves you are not meant for this.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi speaks to Yudhishthira, who is waiting on fate. She says that saying 'I keep working and still do not succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not. Only by not acting is the outcome certain. She is telling him to do right for its own sake and to work as if everything depends on him.
verse.for_you: Your side project is your effort, and it can end two ways, in success or not. The only way to be certain of failure is to stop trying. You are not failing because you are not meant to do this.

verse.speaker: Narrator
verse.setting: Angad plants his foot in Ravana's court and dares anyone to move it; no one can.
verse.sanskrit: भूमि न छाँड़त कपि चरन देखत रिपु मद भाग। कोटि बिघ्न ते संत कर मन जिमि नीति न त्याग ॥
verse.line: A good mind doesn't leave what is right, though a million obstacles come.
verse.translation: The monkey's foot would not leave the ground, and seeing it, the enemy's pride drained away; just as a good person's mind does not abandon what is right, though a million obstacles come.
verse.why: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.

prasang.title: Angad in Ravana's court
prasang.summary: Ram sends Angad as envoy, asking him to speak so the work gets done and it does Ravana good too. In court Ravana insults Angad, his dead father and his lord. Angad bears it, remembering that a lion gains no glory by killing a jackal. At last he plants his foot and dares anyone to move it; no warrior can.
prasang.story_hook: Angad sat down in the enemy's court, and they began to insult his father.
prasang.lesson: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.

verse.meaning: Angad stood in Ravana's court. He was sent by Ram to speak a hard truth, and Ravana answered with insults. Angad felt the sting, but he did not move. He planted his foot on the ground and dared the whole court to lift it. No warrior could. The verse says a good mind holds to what is right, even when a million obstacles come. It is not about winning the argument. It is about standing your ground when the ground itself is shaking.
verse.for_you: You have held your ground through years of care and work, and the doubt has been heavy. Today, hold your purpose in your own life. Let the apps be what they are. You do not have to move them to prove you belong in this space.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the field. He tells him to fight, to act fully, but not to tie his soul to the outcome. Your right is to the work itself. The fruits of that work belong to another force. Do not let the fear of a bad harvest make you stop planting. Do the work completely, and then let the result go.
verse.for_you: You have been trying to build something for years, and the result has not come. Today, do one small thing on the app. Only for the doing. Let the outcome be what it is, and let your mind rest in the work itself.

verse.speaker: Angada
verse.setting: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and failing; young Angada rallies them.
verse.sanskrit: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥
verse.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.
verse.translation: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
verse.why: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

prasang.title: The missed deadline
prasang.summary: The southern search party loses time in a magic cave and misses Sugriva's deadline. Angada rallies them once, then despairs, fearing punishment and certain he will be blamed. Hanuman reasons with him to return.
prasang.story_hook: They came out of the cave to find that spring had already come, and their deadline had gone.
prasang.lesson: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

verse.meaning: Angada speaks to the exhausted monkey search party. They have lost the deadline to find Sita and fear Sugriva’s anger. Angada tells them that those who keep working will surely see the fruit of their work, but once they sink into deep despair, they cannot rise again. The work itself is not the trap. The despair is. He is telling them that the effort must continue because despair makes escape impossible.
verse.for_you: Do one small thing today that is only for you, not for the result. Let the code run or the file save without checking if it works.

story.title: Bhagiratha brings the Ganga down
story.story_hook: Three kings in a row died trying to bring a river down from heaven; the fourth would not stop.
story.summary: King Sagara's sixty thousand sons are burnt to ash; only the Ganga's water can free them. Sagara, his grandson Anshuman and Anshuman's son Dilipa each try and die without success. Bhagiratha finally persists until the river descends, and Brahma honours him for finishing what three generations began.
story.lesson: Some goals take longer than one effort or one lifetime; keep going and others' work is not wasted.

weeks.title: The thing you keep failing at

script: You are tired and quietly defeated. It is the weariness that comes from holding down a job, raising children, and caring for your parents, all while a side project you have returned to for years sits unfinished. You are carrying the weight of a mind that never stops running.

Two childhood friends, Bhasa and Vilasa, meet again as old men after years apart. One asks the other how he is. The other admits he has never found peace. He tells Bhasa that his mind is caught on endless lists, always running through what is done and what must come next. The mind is carried on great waves of tasks, never still. Bhasa said:
उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु, क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम्. इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम्, कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी.
In plain words: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.

The mind keeps a running tally of what is finished, what is happening now, and what is yet to come. This constant accounting exhausts the spirit. Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started. You are not failing because you are lazy. You are failing because your mind has been running on empty for a long time.
Today, let the list rest. You do not need to build anything. You do not need to prove anything. There is no need to count what is done or what must come next. Just let the mind be still for a moment.
Is it possible to be tired and still enough?

depth.life: You are trying to build these apps while the job, the children, and the parents keep taking every last bit of you. The side project sits there unfinished, and the thought of it only adds to the exhaustion.
depth.points: The effort is not the problem. The mind is trapped in a loop of past work, present duty, and future worry. It faints under the weight of the list itself, not the work on the list.
depth.practice: Pick one small task from the list and set a timer for ten minutes. Do only that. When the timer ends, stop. Let the rest of the list wait.
depth.question: What would change if you let the unfinished apps rest for one evening?
